governed_construct: A client-side routing/navigation mechanism used in the file: an import of a routing library (react-router-dom, react-router, wouter, next/router, @reach/router, @tanstack/react-router, etc.) together with the router components, hooks and navigate functions bound to it, or a direct History API navigation call (pushState/replaceState) on an expression bound to window.history.
interpretation: The rule requires that in-app routing be done through react-router-dom. Each routing instance in a file is examined by what it is bound to: router components (BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link, NavLink, Outlet, RouterProvider), hooks (useNavigate, useParams, ...) and helpers (createBrowserRouter, redirect) imported from react-router-dom conform. Routing bound to any other routing package (wouter, next/router, @reach/router, @tanstack/react-router, or the bare react-router package) does not conform, and neither does hand-rolled routing that calls pushState/replaceState on the real window.history object, whether written as window.history.pushState, history.pushState on the global, or through an alias such as const nav = window.history. A file mixing a conforming react-router-dom usage with any non-conforming instance is VIOLATED. A method merely named pushState on a local, unrelated object (e.g. an undo stack called history) is not routing and does not count. Files with no routing or navigation at all are NOT_APPLICABLE. Reading window.location without navigating is not an instance.
